stem: If $|z-(1+2i)|=|z-(-3+4i)|$ and $|z|=5$, then the product of the possible values of $z$ is

verdicts.working: The equidistance condition gives the line y=2x+5. Intersecting with x²+y²=25 gives z=5i and z=-4-3i; their product is 15-20i.

working:
$z=x+iy\Rightarrow |z-(1+2i)|^2=|z-(-3+4i)|^2\Rightarrow y=2x+5$
$x^2+y^2=25\Rightarrow 5x(x+4)=0\Rightarrow z\in\{5i,-4-3i\}$
$(5i)(-4-3i)=15-20i$

Independent check: The equidistance condition gives the line y=2x+5. Intersecting with x²+y²=25 gives z=5i and z=-4-3i; their product is 15-20i.
solution:
Let $z=x+iy$. The equidistance condition gives the perpendicular bisector $y=2x+5$. Using $|z|=5$:
$$x^2+(2x+5)^2=25\Rightarrow 5x(x+4)=0,$$
so $z=5i$ or $z=-4-3i$. Their product is $(5i)(-4-3i)=15-20i$.
